judgments.title: PENGERANG REFINING COMPANY SDN. BHD. v MAJLIS PERBANDARAN PENGERANG
judgments.catchwords: Administrative Law – Judicial review – Duty of candour – Public authority – Duty to make full and fair disclosure of all material facts – Failure to disclose that Valuation List being amended had expired – Breach of duty of candour – Consequences. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Statutory lifespan – Section 137 Local Government Act 1976 – New Valuation List must be prepared once every five years – Valuation List expires after five years – No local authority may use Valuation List for indeterminable period. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Amendment – Section 144 Local Government Act 1976 – Amendment can only be made to current Valuation List – Not to expired or outdated Valuation List – Amendment to expired list is ultra vires and void. Local Government Law – Valuation List – Section 137(2) – Saving provision – Valuation List remains in force until superseded by new list – Not a power to extend lifespan of existing list – Only temporary measure while new list being prepared– Extension of time – Section 137(3) – State Authority may extend period for preparation of new Valuation List – Not power to extend validity of existing Valuation List – No extension granted in present case. Local Government Law – Retrospective rates – Amendment to current Valuation List may have retrospective effect – But no retrospective effect where Valuation List itself has expired – Question of retrospectivity becomes academic.

CRIMINAL LAW (DANGEROUS DRUGS) CRIMINAL LAW: Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 – Section 39A(2)(d) – Possession – Consolidated charge combining weights of heroin and monoacetylmorphines – Single transaction – Whether separate drug types recovered from the same physical transaction must be charged under distinct counts – Binding precedential force of the Court of Appeal in Abd Talib bin Bakri lwn Pendakwa Raya [2020] 3 MLJ 777 – Purpose of aggregation – Prevention of consecutive, compounding statutory double-presumptions under the Act – Protection of equality before the law under Article 8(1) of the Federal Constitution. 2. CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (REVISION & INHERENT POWERS) CRIMINAL PROCEDURE: Revision – Powers of High Court – Supervisory and revisionary jurisdiction – Criminal Procedure Code, s. 323 – Courts of Judicature Act 1964, ss. 31, 35(1) – Sessions Court Judge summarily discharging accused under a Discharge Not Amounting to Acquittal (DNAA) on a mention date – Preliminary objection regarding the structure of the charge sheet – Whether subordinate courts possess inherent power to abort trials or strike out valid charges – Distinction between inherent jurisdiction of superior courts and limited statutory jurisdiction of subordinate judiciaries – Application of Karpal Singh & Anor v. Public Prosecutor [1991] 2 MLJ 544. 3. CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (JOINT TRIAL & TRANSFER) CRIMINAL PROCEDURE: Trial – Joint trial – Criminal Procedure Code, s. 170 – Same transaction doctrine – Application by the prosecution to try a reinstated Section 39A(2) Sessions Court charge jointly with a Section 12(2) Magistrate's Court minor charge – Offences arising from the same narcotics raid – Unity of time, place, community of purpose and continuity of action – Duplication of witnesses and chemist testimonies – Whether separate trials create a risk of inconsistent findings of fact – Proper administration of justice – Criminal Procedure Code, s. 417. 4. CONSTITUTIONAL LAW (SEPARATION OF POWERS) CONSTITUTIONAL LAW: Public Prosecutor – Executive discretion – Federal Constitution, art. 145(3) – Absolute control and direction of criminal prosecutions – Framing and preference of charges – Whether subordinate courts can interfere with the prosecutorial choice of charges – Separation of powers – Courts as gatekeepers of statutory legality vs. directors of prosecution – Application of Long bin Samad & Ors. v. Public Prosecutor [1974] 2 MLJ 152. 5. STATUTORY INTERPRETATION (RULES OF CONSTRUCTION) STATUTORY INTERPRETATION: Rules of construction – Literal rule – Purposive approach – Interpretation Acts 1948 and 1967, s. 17A – Phrase "a total of 5 grammes or more in weight of heroin, morphine and monoacetylmorphines" – Conjunctive word "and" – Explicit statutory authorisation to aggregate weights of specified substances – Whether court has power to fill statutory gaps or rewrite clear penal provisions under the guise of equity – Application of Gan Joon Zin v. Fong Kui Lun & Ors [2004] 4 CLJ 729. 6.
